cues.text: The anatomy of an L L M. What you are actually buying, in under three minutes.
When you send a message, the model never sees just your question.
The system prompt, the whole conversation, retrieved documents and tool outputs are stitched into one long context. And all of it is billed.
A tokenizer chops that text into sub-word pieces called tokens, and each one becomes a number.
"The cat sat on the" is five tokens. Tokens are the unit on your invoice.
Each number then looks up a vector of thousands of values. Meaning, encoded as geometry.
Those vectors flow through a stack of about eighty identical transformer layers.
Inside every layer, attention lets each token look back at the ones before it. The last "the" pulls hardest on "sat" and "cat".
At the top of the stack, the model scores every one of a hundred thousand possible next tokens. "Mat" wins, and a sampler picks it.
Then that token is fed straight back in, and the whole stack runs again. One full pass, for every word you see streaming onto your screen.
That loop splits every request into two phases.
Prefill reads your entire prompt in one parallel pass. Fast, and cheap.
Decode writes the answer one token at a time, and every token re-reads all of the model's weights from memory.
That is why output tokens cost three to eight times more than input.
The same physics makes the discounts honest. Cached prompts skip re-reading, for about ninety percent off. Batch lanes run at half price.
Finally, five hidden dials quietly change your bill. Two are set by the model maker, two by whoever serves the model, and one is yours.
One. The tokenizer. The same sentence costs almost seven times more tokens in Hindi than in English.
Two. Architecture. A trillion-parameter mixture of experts wakes up only about thirty-seven billion per token, so it can be cheaper than a dense seventy-billion model.
Three. Precision. Going from sixteen bits to eight, to four, halves the memory read per token, each step.
Four. Batching. Thirty-two requests share one read of the weights, cutting cost per token by over ninety percent. The biggest lever of all.
And five. The context you send. Your system prompt is re-sent, and re-billed, on every single turn.
Sequential generation. Memory. Weight reads. That is the machine behind every price in this guide.
Now open each chapter, and try the dials yourself.
